subject: Post-call: Dedicated SLO pilot scope, streaming/conv. requirements, and hardware reckon
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Thompson <sara.thompson@helixhealth.com>, Tom Riley <tom.riley@helixhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2026 13:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Dedicated SLO pilot scope, streaming/conv. requirements, and hardware reckon

Hi Sara / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the call this morning. Quick recap from our side and a proposed lightweight pilot scope so we can validate SLO fit for dedicated capacity. I captured action items, assumptions, and a recommended hardware shortlist below.

High-level goal
- Validate a Dedicated capacity that meets Helix Health's real-time assist use case for clinical chart summarization (streaming output to UI) with p95 latency target and predictable cost.

Key constraints you called out
- Typical request sizes: ~180 tokens input, ~220 tokens output (average).
- Peak concurrency: spikes to ~50 concurrent interactive sessions during morning shift; typical sustained concurrency ~12–18.
- Streaming required for progressive sentence-level flush to UI; max per-token latency target important.

Initial SLO targets (proposed for pilot)
- p50 latency (streaming start): < 80 ms after first token generation
- p95 end-to-end (full response complete): < 350 ms for up-to-220-token responses under sustained concurrency of 16
- Sustained throughput target for pilot: ~80 reqs/minute (1.3 rps) steady per-node; burstable to 300 rps cluster-wide during peak windows with autoscale policy
- KV prefix cache hit expectation: ~45% for repeated chart templates

Pilot scope (1 week load + smoke + acceptance run)
- Week 0: baseline model run on Hosted with sample workload (sanitized data)
- Week 1: Dedicated pilot on a 2-node reserved slab, run load profiles (ramping concurrency, long tail tests) and collect p50/p95/p99 latencies, token throughput, GPU utilization, memory/KV metrics
- Acceptance criteria: p95 below 350ms for 220-token outputs and stable 95% of test windows meeting target; no OOM or >10% dropped requests under steady-state test.

Hardware shortlist (qualitative recommendation)
- Option A: H100-80GB (best throughput for long contexts + streaming with large KV) — recommended for aggressive concurrency and long-tail stability
- Option B: A100-80GB (balanced cost/perf) — good fit if quantization used and less KV pressure
- Option C: L4-48GB (cost-efficient for lower concurrency, quicker cold-starts but smaller KV limits)

Initial ask from Helix (action items)
- Confirm average and 95th percentile tokens for input and output (you gave averages, please share 95p).
- Provide a sanitized prompt set and 30-minute sample trace for one week of traffic (we'll use for load replays).
- Confirm compliance constraints for pilot data (we will route through your VPC for Private/Dedicated if needed).

Attachments: I attached a short pilot matrix and a preliminary SLO requirements workbook.

Next steps
1) You: share 95p token numbers + sample traces by Wed, Jul 21.
2) Us: return a pilot runbook and final hardware recommendation (by Thu, Jul 22) after we see token distribution.
3) If acceptance criteria look good, open SOW to reserve a pilot slab for two weeks.

Thanks — I looped Karthik and Lauren for ops/hardware math.

— Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai
Attachments: slo_requirements.xlsx (spreadsheet stub), pilot-matrix.csv (csv stub)

From: Sara Thompson <sara.thompson@helixhealth.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Riley <tom.riley@helixhealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Dedicated SLO pilot scope, streaming/conv. requirements, and hardware reckon

Thanks Sergio — this looks good and thorough. Quick clarifications:
- 95p sizes: input 320 tokens, output 480 tokens (we have longer summaries for some cases).
- Peak concurrency: earlier I under-quoted — our busiest coder shift can see up to 70 concurrent interactive sessions for short bursts (~10–15 minutes), sustained daytime concurrency remains ~18.
- Compliance: sample traces will be fully de-identified but still considered PHI until we sign a DPA for the pilot; we can route via VPC connector in your Private option.

We will upload sanitized traces and the 95p token distribution by EOD Wed (Jul 21). Could you include a rough reserve-cost delta for H100 vs A100 for the pilot order of magnitude in your runbook? That will help procurement.

Also, can you confirm if the streaming p50 <80ms target is measured from the first server byte or from model token generation start? We need consistency for our benchmarking.

Sara Thompson
Head of Product, Helix Health
sara.thompson@helixhealth.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Thompson <sara.thompson@helixhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2026 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Dedicated SLO pilot scope, streaming/conv. requirements, and hardware reckon

Sergio / team — quick cost/perf sketch based on Sara's 95p numbers (input 320 / output 480):
- H100-80GB: higher throughput headroom; estimate for pilot slab (2-node reserved for 1 week) ~ $28k–$34k (includes license/reservation uplift + monitoring). Best for headroom at 70-concurrency spikes.
- A100-80GB: ~ $18k–$22k for the same slab; acceptable if we use 8-bit/4-bit quantization on model variants and enable aggressive KV caching. Slightly higher p95 risk on long responses.
- L4-48GB: ~ $6k–$9k, but will likely fail to meet p95 on the 480-token tail at 70-concurrency spikes unless we shard requests / lower concurrency. Good lower-cost pilot if Helix confines traffic to simulated windows.

On the streaming p50 question: we measure p50 streaming start from the first server byte emitted (includes request routing + model generation). For absolute model-only generation time we can add a second metric (model-token-start) in the runbook. Recommend we publish both so you can disambiguate network vs model behavior.

I'll draft the pilot runbook with cost bands and a test matrix. Lauren — can you take ops on the acceptance test definitions and the run schedule? Grace — please prepare a short benchmark plan for KV hit-rate tuning.

—Karthik

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Thompson <sara.thompson@helixhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2026 08:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Dedicated SLO pilot scope, streaming/conv. requirements, and hardware reckon

Adding the ops checklist and acceptance test cadence:
- Pre-pilot: deploy pilot infra in Helix VPC (secure connector), baseline smoke with 10 synthetic sessions, verify KV persistence and logging.
- Day 1–2: ramp test to 18 sustained concurrency, run 2x 30-minute windows at expected daytime load, collect metrics.
- Day 3: peak burst test — ramp to 70 concurrency for three 10-minute bursts, observe degradation and failovers.
- Day 4–5: tuning window — KV hit policy, batching thresholds, quantization profile A/B.
- Acceptance run: 2-hour steady run at sustained 16 concurrency + two 10-minute peak bursts at 70; acceptance if 95% of 10-minute windows meet p95 criteria.

Logs & artifacts we will produce for sign-off: full perf trace, kernel-level GPU utilization summaries, token-level latency histograms, and a short conformance report.

I will attach the run schedule to the runbook (will link into the shared Drive).

— Lauren

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Post-call: Dedicated SLO pilot scope, streaming/conv. requirements, and hardware reckon

Sara / Tom — perfect, thanks for the token numbers and the DPA note. We're scheduling internal prep today. Next concrete items for you:
1) Upload sanitized traces + 95p token distribution to the Drive link by EOD today if possible.
2) Review the attached runbook (I included cost bands from Karthik and the ops cadence from Lauren).
3) If you want H100 headroom, mark that preference on the M.A.P. — procurement will want a cost sign-off before we provision.

We'll circulate a signed pilot SOW draft once we confirm VPC connector timing. I'll also include explicit metrics definitions (p50-stream-start vs model-only) so our acceptance testing is apples-to-apples.

If there's anything else, flag it on this thread and we'll handle it. Looking forward to getting the pilot greenlit.

— Sergio
